title: Special Token Exploitation Prevalence: How Many Open Models Are Vulnerable?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: special token injection is a documented vulnerability; mapping its prevalence across open models produces a ranked vulnerability list that practitioners can act on immediately. Clear, specific impact.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Enumerating special tokens and crafting injection attacks requires understanding tokenizers and chat templates, but these are well-documented. The methodology is scripting-heavy rather than ML-heavy. Guided beginners can execute with mentor help.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: a vulnerability matrix of models vs. special token attacks. Systematic but straightforward scripting task. Can be tightly scoped to 5-6 models and fits in 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: MetaBreak (arXiv:2510.10271, 2025) identifies four attack primitives based on special token manipulation and tests against online LLMs. The LangGrinch CVE (CVE-2025-68664) demonstrates real-world special token exploitation. OWASP LLM Top 10 2025 includes prompt injection as the #1 risk. However, a systematic prevalence survey mapping which specific special token attacks work against which open-source models (a vulnerability matrix) is not directly available in published work. MetaBreak covers online/proprietary models; the open-model systematic survey adds value.

evidence: MetaBreak: Jailbreaking Online LLM Services via Special Token Manipulation. arXiv:2510.10271, 2025.
